answer: A strong defence is escalating proof-of-work identity issuance: every new agent must solve a computational puzzle before joining, and the puzzle difficulty doubles for each extra identity created from the same device or network fingerprint. One honest agent pays a trivial cost, like a bee sipping nectar, but a Sybil farmer minting thousands of fakes faces a bill that grows exponentially, far beyond any ivory-tower budget, while timber-solid economics make bulk forgery unprofitable: the attacker burns far more compute than any fake identity could ever earn, so mass creation stops paying.
